=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:1010-1015 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The heal-scope entry `agents.d/<N>-*.md` is a bare glob that admits names such as `agents.d/8064-.md` or `agents.d/8064-a b.md`, which the stricter `is_own_issue_fragment` rejects. The same shape appears in scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:946 and scripts/implement_heal_preflight.sh:132.
  WHY: A heal editor can write malformed fragment names into the credentialed host checkout, and only CI fragment folding backstops it. All reviewers rated this NIT.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:2881-2884 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The step-summary else branch still says "A maintainer can review the plan and reply `/approved`" for `heal_scope_plan_out_of_scope`. This contradicts the new hold comment at lines 2722-2723, which says `/approved` alone does not help.
  WHY: A maintainer who follows the summary posts `/approved`, and implement refuses the files under the frozen heal scope marker. Severity disagreement: MAJOR (sonnet, minimax, qwen) vs NIT (gpt-6-luna, glm).
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:2718 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The directory/glob note "reply `/approved` instead" is rendered without a `$reason` condition. It fires for heal holds, so the same comment also carries the line 2723 text saying `/approved` alone does not help.
  WHY: One comment gives contradictory next steps and sends the maintainer to the dead end the PR set out to remove. Severity disagreement: MAJOR (sonnet, minimax) vs NIT (gpt-6-luna, glm).
- scripts/validation_harness_sandbox.sh:944-955 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `stage_from_head` falls back silently to the working-tree copy when `git ls-tree` or `git cat-file` fails, with no log line.
  WHY: A transient git error reintroduces the #7913 behaviour with no trace. Severity disagreement: MAJOR (gemini) vs NIT (sonnet, glm, minimax hardening suggestion).
- changelog.d/8064-heal-scope-own-agents-fragment.md:1 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The PR adds two changelog fragments (this file and changelog.d/8064-validation-sandbox-support-from-head.md) although the convention is one fragment per PR.
  WHY: `scripts/assemble_changelog.py` folds each fragment independently, so release assembly produces two entries for one PR.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:17028-17036 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `_plan_auto_approval_gate` calls the guard without `--heal-scope-file`. Stall recovery can therefore approve a heal plan that plan.yml holds as out of scope.
  WHY: Planner gate and resolver logic diverge, so implement can burn a run and then refuse the files. Severity disagreement: MAJOR (gemini) vs NIT (glm). Sonnet and minimax noted the same divergence as pre-existing #7444 behaviour that this PR does not introduce.
- scripts/validation_harness_sandbox.sh:928-962 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: `stage_from_head` runs raw git operations in a directory context that may not be fully initialized or protected during sandbox staging.
  WHY: Fallback is silent on git failure, so explicit failure reporting would improve observability.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

A branch changing the renderer or a template together with its tests still tests main's copy. Severity: MAJOR (minimax, glm) vs NIT (sonnet, qwen). Sonnet notes the PR description names only four files, so this may be a scope question.

  WHY: A transient git failure could leave untrusted working-tree bytes in the sandbox instead of committed HEAD bytes, bypassing the #7913 hardening.

- scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:1010-1015, scripts/implement_heal_preflight.sh:131-133, scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:944-947 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The heal-scope entry is the bare glob `agents.d/<N>-*.md`, looser than the strict `is_own_issue_fragment` regex (scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py:511-516). It admits `agents.d/8064-.md`, `agents.d/8064-a b.md`, `agents.d/8064-;x.md` and `agents.d/8064-..md`.
  WHY: A heal editor can write a malformed name that the commit guard (`implement_commit_changes.sh:576-587`) lets through and `assemble_agents.py` then folds. The blast radius is bounded, so this is a shape inconsistency and not a new capability.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:2881-2885 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The step summary for `heal_scope_plan_out_of_scope` still falls into the generic else branch ("A maintainer can review the plan and reply `/approved`"), while the new comment (plan.yml:2722-2723) says `/approved` alone does not help.
  WHY: A maintainer who follows the step summary replies `/approved` and implement refuses the out-of-scope files.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:2718 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The directory/glob note is rendered without a `$reason` condition and fires for heal holds whose denied_paths include a directory or glob, so the comment carries both "reply `/approved` instead" and "`/approved` alone does not help".
  WHY: The comment no longer states a single actionable next step, and it sends the maintainer to the dead end PR item 3 set out to close.
